reference: Generalised Bateman solution for branching decay networks, written as a sum over simple paths and evaluated in 60-digit arithmetic (mpmath), cross-checked against mpmath.expm of the same generator - two structurally different algorithms that agree to 5e-44. The one-step activation cases use the closed-form solution of the two-species constant-flux system with target burn-up, also in 60-digit arithmetic. Equilibrium cases use the exact finite-time two-member ratio and quote the asymptotic limit lambda_d/(lambda_d - lambda_p). Nuclear data are the IAEA Live Chart / ENSDF ground-state snapshot, quoted per case.
reference_citations: H. Bateman, 'The solution of a system of differential equations occurring in the theory of radioactive transformations', Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 15 (1910) 423.
M. Pusa, 'Higher-Order Chebyshev Rational Approximation Method and Application to Burnup Equations', Nucl. Sci. Eng. 182 (2016) 297 - the method the tool implements.

IAEA Live Chart of Nuclides / ENSDF, relnsd API, ground-state snapshot (Extraction_date 2023-10-18), used both to rebuild the missing data file and as the source of every half-life and branching ratio quoted here.
K. Way and E. P. Wigner / standard secular-equilibrium algebra: A_d/A_p -> lambda_d/(lambda_d - lambda_p).
tolerance: 1e-9 relative on the network evolution: CRAM48 is a rational approximation to the matrix exponential whose published accuracy for burnup matrices is around 1e-14, the reference is exact to 60 digits and the tool exports full double precision, so anything looser would not be testing the solver. Species holding less than 1e-12 of the network's atoms are recorded but not graded relatively, because there the float64 solver carries absolute, not relative, accuracy. 1e-12 on atom conservation and on the activity = ln(2) N / T_1/2 identity, which are exact arithmetic. 2e-4 on the activation panel, which prints five significant digits. 1e-6 on the equilibrium activity ratio.
environment: Chromium (Playwright) against a local HTTP overlay of /root/site with the reconstructed fixture bench/fixtures/nuclide-data.FIXTURE.js in place of the missing nuclide-data.js. Node v22.22.2.
data_file_caveat: The deployed nuclide-data.js and neutron-data/ are NOT present in this tree. Everything below was measured against a ground-state fixture rebuilt from the IAEA Live Chart API (same snapshot date, 2023-10-18, that the tool's manifest quotes), with no metastable, decay-gamma or fission-yield overlay. This benchmark therefore says nothing about the integrity, completeness or provenance of the data the deployed page actually loads; it tests the mathematics the page applies to whatever data it is given.

not_benchmarked.deployed_data_file: nuclide-data.js is absent, so its record count, metastable overlay, decay-gamma overlay, evaluated fission yields, decay-energy model and QA counters could not be checked at all.
not_benchmarked.fendl_cross_sections: neutron-data/ is absent, so the FENDL-3.2c pointwise layer, the group-average calculator and the WASM cross-section kernel could not be exercised.
not_benchmarked.gamma_spectrum_and_dose: Both are driven entirely by overlays that live in the missing data file; with the fixture they have nothing to show, so grading them would be grading the fixture.
not_benchmarked.fission_yields: The bundled evaluated fission-yield sets live in the missing data file.
not_benchmarked.monte_carlo_uncertainty: The uncertainty propagation samples half-lives from their ENSDF uncertainties with a seeded RNG; its output is a distribution, and the fixture does not carry the same uncertainty set as the deployed file, so it is not graded here.
not_benchmarked.xenon_dynamics: The reactor Xe-135 panel duplicates the site's own xenon.html, which is benchmarked separately; it is out of scope for this pass.

CRAM48 evolution of the 3-nuclide network reached from Sr-90 (Sr-90 -> Y-90 -> Zr-90) at 1000 s. Atom conservation: every branch of every member of this network ends inside the network, so the sum of all species must stay at the initial atom count for ever. This is a property of the equations, not of the data, and it is what a silent truncation of a decay branch would break.

provenance_note: Reference values are derived by bench-src/ref/gen_nuclideatlas.py rather than transcribed, but that generator cannot be re-run anywhere in this programme: it reads bench-src/fixtures/nuclide-data.FIXTURE.js, which is present in no tree (the whole filesystem was searched for it on 2026-10-15). The corpus is reused as stored, which AGENTS section 5 classes as a regression reference, so reference_provenance reads recorded and not recomputed: a reused stored reference can show that a build changed a number and can never show the number was wrong to begin with.
